name: Organized Noize
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 crunk — Organized Noize (Rico Wade, Ray Murray, Sleepy Brown)
Billboard — The Art of Organized Noize (https://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/hip-hop/7272547/the-art-of-organized-noize-documentary-film)
notes: ⛔ **This is the board the archetype was written from, so the risk here is an entry that restates its parent.** What it authors instead is the trio's *own* paragraph read tighter than the lane the parent had to cover. Four places it is narrower or different. (1) **The band, not the lane.** 70–92 with mode 80, against the parent's 68–100/84 — the parent had to stretch to hold OutKast's rave tempi and Big Boi's faster funk cuts; this paragraph gives one band and this file states only that band. (2) **8th hats, not a spread.** The paragraph says 8th hats outright, so `hihat.base` weights 8ths 5:2 over 16ths where the parent sits at 4:3 — this is the producer whose records the 16th weighting came from *elsewhere*. Tambourine and congas are named as *standing layers* and are the only two perc lanes here, at [2,4] rather than the parent's five lanes at [1,4]. (3) **The changes move.** "4-bar loops with genuine changes" is `harmonicRhythm` weighted 5:3:2 toward `1_per_bar` and `chordDurationBeats` [2,6] rather than the parent's [2,8]: this board changes chord more often than the container it defines. The named families lead — ii–V motion at weight 5 and the plagal IV–I tag at 4 — and `extensions` are 82% coloured for the minor 7/9 vamps. (4) **The walk is chromatic.** `bassline.cellShapes` are replaced with ascending/descending walks and the passing-tone set carries m2 and M3, for "walking motion and chromatic passing tones"; `followRootsProb` 0.42 is below the parent's 0.5 because a walking player leaves the root more often than the container's average. Sleepy Brown's sung hooks are the countermelody at `densityRatio` 0.68 with `fillGapsOnly` false, and the "4-bar phrases with countermelody" is `melody.phraseBars` weighted 5:3:2 toward 4. The subtractive method — "go in and take some stuff out" — is the long instrumental intro that plays without drums, the instrumental outro, and `switchUpProb` down at 0.22, because sections here "change by instrument entry/exit rather than by fills". ⚠ **Confidence is medium and the inferred parameter is the tempo.** The research rates the paragraph high-medium: the subtractive philosophy, the live instrumentation and the full-album credits are sourced, but the band is marked [LOW-CONF] and mode 80 inside it is mine. ⚠ `bass808` stays the parent's `counter_riff` role and is pushed to [18,33] with `slideProb` 0.05 — the research says the booty-bass sub is added *beneath rather than instead*, and `counter_riff` is the only role that lets the played bass keep sounding. This model's fill band is `smallEveryBars` 2 / `bigEveryBars` 4 with a 16th/32nd strong-weak roll; inside it, `gapProb` 0.52, `descendProb` 0.22 and `rampJitter` 13 are its own, so it does not write the archetype's fill even though it wrote the archetype. ⚠ **`lockTo808` raised from 0.3 to 0.61.** The 808 takes each kick with this probability, and at 0.3 over this model's 8-kick floor a seed could produce no 808 at all — which `bass808.rs` refuses, because a declared 808 that sometimes vanishes is a part a producer cannot rely on. It is still well under a lock: a good share of kicks carry no sub. ⚠ The chord voicing moved up to [51, 84] so the bass stays under the harmony — it started at 44 against a bass reaching 50, an overlap of 7. The span is preserved; a voicing that low was competing with the bass rather than sitting over it. ⚠ `countermelody.registerOffset` moved from -3 to -12: inside a fifth the counter sits in the melody's own register and plays its pitches at the same moment, which `coherence.rs` calls a second lead rather than an answer. ⚠ `countermelody.fillGapsOnly` returned to true. With it off and a density of 0.68, the counter plays THROUGH the melody rather than around it, and coherence.rs measures that as the counter sounding the melody own pitch at the same moment — a second lead rather than an answer. The register offset and the styles are untouched; what changed is that it waits its turn.
